report_name: Lazarus APT Uses AI and Post-Quantum Crypto in New Campaign

threat_actors.name: Lazarus Group
threat_actors.description: North Korea-linked APT group conducting the 'Operation FlashHole' cyberespionage campaign against South Korean entities, utilizing AI-generated content, legitimate software abuse, and post-quantum cryptography for C2 communications.
threat_actors.goals: Cyberespionage, targeting intellectual property and sensitive corporate data from key South Korean industries.

attack_patterns.name: Spearphishing Link
attack_patterns.description: Lazarus Group sent highly targeted spear-phishing emails containing links to fraudulent websites, such as fake employee portfolios created with AI tools, to gain initial access.

attack_patterns.name: System Binary Proxy Execution
attack_patterns.description: The legitimate South Korean software 'CrossWeb EX' was abused to load and execute malicious payloads, bypassing security controls.

attack_patterns.name: Symmetric Cryptography
attack_patterns.description: The LPEClient backdoor used the ML-KEM-1024 (Kyber) post-quantum cryptography algorithm to establish a secure, symmetrically encrypted command-and-control channel resilient to future decryption.

attack_patterns.name: Generative AI
attack_patterns.description: AI tools were used by the Lazarus Group to generate convincing content, including profile pictures and text, for fraudulent websites used in spear-phishing lures.

malware.name: TouchHub
malware.description: A malware tool used in Operation FlashHole for executing commands and deploying further malware payloads.

malware.name: ClientHub
malware.description: A malware component used in Operation FlashHole involved in malware deployment and command-and-control operations.

malware.name: LPEClient
malware.description: An updated backdoor used by the Lazarus Group that incorporates the ML-KEM-1024 (Kyber) post-quantum cryptography algorithm to establish a secure command-and-control channel.

tools.name: CrossWeb EX
tools.description: A legitimate South Korean web authentication and security software solution that was abused by the Lazarus Group to load malicious payloads as part of the Operation FlashHole campaign.

campaigns.name: Operation FlashHole
campaigns.description: A sophisticated cyberespionage campaign by the Lazarus Group, active since July 2025, targeting organizations in South Korea. It is characterized by the use of AI-generated phishing lures, abuse of legitimate software, and post-quantum cryptography for C2.
campaigns.objective: Cyberespionage against South Korean construction, software, and manufacturing sectors.

identities.name: South Korean organizations
identities.description: Organizations in South Korea's construction, software, and wire-communication equipment manufacturing sectors targeted by the Lazarus Group in Operation FlashHole for cyberespionage.

identities.name: NIST
identities.description: The U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology, which standardized the ML-KEM-1024 (Kyber) algorithm used by the Lazarus Group.

infrastructure.name: Lazarus C2 Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: Command and control infrastructure, likely using newly registered or dynamic DNS domains, used by the LPEClient backdoor with post-quantum cryptography encryption.

indicators.name: Lazarus Abused Tool CrossWebEX.exe
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: Lazarus Abused Tool - CrossWebEX.exe
id: c6b5a493-82e1-4c0b-9a8f-7e6d5c4a3b2a
status: experimental
description: Detects the presence or execution of CrossWebEX.exe, a legitimate tool abused by the Lazarus Group in Operation FlashHole.
references:
  - https://securelist.com/lazarus-operation-flashhole/121541/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-21
tags:
  - attack.t1218
level: informational
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\CrossWebEX.exe'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the presence or execution of CrossWebEX.exe, a legitimate but abused software.

indicators.name: Suspicious Child Process of CrossWebEX.exe
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Child Process of CrossWebEX.exe
id: f9a8b7c6-d5e4-4f3a-2b1c-0a9f8e7d6c5b
status: experimental
description: Detects the legitimate 'CrossWebEX.exe' process spawning command-line interpreters, which may indicate abuse by the Lazarus Group as seen in Operation FlashHole.
references:
  - https://securelist.com/lazarus-operation-flashhole/121541/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-21
tags:
  - attack.t1218
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.execution
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\CrossWebEX.exe'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
  condition: all of selection_*
indicators.description: Detects CrossWebEX.exe spawning command shells, a TTP of Lazarus in this campaign.

indicators.name: Suspicious File Modification in SoftForum Directory
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious File Modification in SoftForum Directory
id: e8d7c6b5-a4f3-4e2d-1c0b-9a8f7e6d5c4a
status: experimental
description: Monitors for new or modified files in the 'C:\Program Files\SoftForum\' directory, the default installation path for CrossWeb software, which was abused by Lazarus in Operation FlashHole.
references:
  - https://securelist.com/lazarus-operation-flashhole/121541/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-21
tags:
  - attack.t1218
  - attack.defense_evasion
level: medium
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|startswith: 'C:\Program Files\SoftForum\'
  filter_legit:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\CrossWebEX.exe'
      - '\updater.exe'
  condition: selection and not filter_legit
indicators.description: Detects file modifications in the CrossWeb EX installation directory, a potential sign of tampering.

indicators.name: ML-KEM-1024 PQC Algorithm String
indicators.pattern:
title: Potential LPEClient Malware with PQC
id: d7c6b5a4-93e2-4d1c-0b9a-8f7e6d5c4a3b
status: experimental
description: Detects files containing the string 'ML-KEM-1024', potentially indicating the LPEClient backdoor used by Lazarus Group, which employs post-quantum cryptography. This rule requires a log source capable of file content inspection.
references:
  - https://securelist.com/lazarus-operation-flashhole/121541/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-21
tags:
  - attack.t1573.001
  - attack.command_and_control
level: medium
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Contents|contains: 'ML-KEM-1024'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the string 'ML-KEM-1024' in file contents, which is associated with the LPEClient backdoor's PQC implementation.
